The material used was induction melted from pure elements in alumina crucibles under Ar atmosphere. Parallel-epiped samples of width and thickness 25 mm and length 50 mm were obtained by drop casting into a Cu mould.

other.melting: induction melted from pure elements in alumina crucibles

evidence.quote: The material used was induction melted from pure elements in alumina crucibles under Ar atmosphere. Parallel-epiped samples of width and thickness 25 mm and length 50 mm were obtained by drop casting into a Cu mould.

parameters.deformation: strain of ~0.1 per blow, initial height reduction 0.3, repeated to accumulated strain ~4

evidence.quote: Forging was carried out at 1150 °C, following tests at 1000 °C and 1100 °C which showed immediate fracture or eventual fracture at increasing strain levels. Forging was carried out using a high-speed press which imposed a strain of ~0.1 per blow in ~1 s
This procedure was repeated many times, until accumulated strains of four and six were achieved, when the samples were long bars of small square cross section.
At the end of straining, the sample bars were reheated a final time, again for 10 min at 1150 °C, to ensure recrystallization, and plunged into a sand bath to ensure slow cooling.

attributes.size: rod-shaped particles ~10 µm wide and 50 µm long

evidence.quote: Examination of the boride particles by electron diffraction in the TEM showed diffraction patterns corresponding to the Nb5B6 and Nb3B4 phases

attributes.size: domain size as large as the grain size

evidence.quote: All the crept samples examined contained a moderate dislocation density, with these dislocations often present as tangles close to and around the particles. Examination by weak beam techniques showed that these were superdislocations composed of two partials, as would be expected for deformation in the B2 ordered material present at the high creep temperatures [38].

Consistent with this was the confirmation by electron diffraction of strong B2 order, with large corresponding domain size (as large as the grain size), and some DO3 order with a fine domain size (~30 nm) corresponding to order created during cooling after creep.
A few of the particles, seen light in Fig. 1c, contained considerable amounts of C with a chemistry corresponding to NbCB2.
The as-cast material has a columnar grain structure ~200–300 lm wide containing a cellular segregation structure with cell wall spacing of ~40–50 lm (see Fig. 1a).
First, the grains became equiaxed, of size ~30 lm, and showed a weak h110i texture along the bar axis.
The as-cast material has a columnar grain structure ~200–300 lm wide containing a cellular segregation structure with cell wall spacing of ~40–50 lm (see Fig. 1a).

The original segregation cell walls have been transformed into boundaries of relatively low misorientation, as indicated by the similarity of diffraction contrast across the boundaries, which are decorated with the 0.2–0.7 lm particle fragments (see Figs. 7 and 8).

Binary Fe–Al and ternary Fe–Al–Cr alloys of similar compositions to the matrix of the present material show stress exponents of 3–4 when tested at similar temperatures and strain rates, characteristic of deformation controlled by dislocation glide and climb [3,39].
The resulting material retains a coarse grain size with a refined dispersion of fine boride particles.

Such values correspond to those expected when dislocation motion between forest dislocations controls strain, in agreement with the high work hardening observed for these strain rates and temperatures.
The values of friction stress deduced here are related below to estimations of boundary strength based on the Orowan particle-strengthening mechanism.

The strength of both the particle-hardened walls and the dispersion-strengthened near-wall regions may be estimated using the Orowan strengthening model, since in both cases the particles are large and uncuttable.

The lower values found at higher temperatures indicate that there is additional thermal activation of the controlling mechanisms, such as diﬀusion, climb over particles and detachment of dislocations from particles.
